en: Even if one possesses a beautiful body, or likewise a wife, a charming and varied reputation, and wealth equal to Mount Meru—
if the mind is not fixed upon the lotus feet of the Guru, [all is in vain].
What then? What then? What then? What then? ||1||
Wife, wealth, sons, grandsons, and all else that has arisen in the home— all these kinsmen are indeed born [of this]; yet,
if the mind is not fixed upon the lotus-feet of the Guru, [all is in vain].
Then what? Then what? Then what? Then what? ||2||
Vedic knowledge with its six limbs and the like resides in the mouth as scriptural learning, and it produces prose and excellent verse such as poetry;
yet, if the mind is not fixed upon the lotus-feet of the Guru, [it remains fruitless].
Then what? Then what? Then what? Then what? ||3||
Honored abroad and blessed in one's own land, there is none other than I in matters of virtuous conduct; yet,
if the mind is not fixed upon the lotus-feet of the Guru, [all is in vain].
What then? What then? What then? What then? ||4||
If the mind is not fixed upon the lotus-feet of the Guru, whose lotus-feet are always served by hosts of kings and princes throughout the circle of the earth;
What then? What then? What then? What then? ||5||
My fame has spread in all directions through the power of my generosity, and by his grace, every object in the world is in my hand; yet,
this would not be so if my mind were not fixed upon the lotus-feet of the Guru.
Then what? Then what? Then what? Then what? ||6||

If the mind is not attached to enjoyments, nor to yoga, nor even to the king of horses, nor to the face of a beloved, nor indeed to riches— if the mind is not clinging to the lotus-feet of the Guru— then [it is well].
What then? What then? What then? What then? ||7||

Whether in the forest or in my own home, whether in action or in the body, my mind does not dwell upon anything other than Your priceless self. If the mind is not fixed upon the lotus feet of the Guru, [it will wander].
What then? What then? What then? What then? ||8||
The meritorious person— whether an ascetic, a king, a celibate student, or a householder— who recites this *Gurvaṣṭaka*,
shall obtain his desired object and the state known as Brahman.
He whose mind is fixed upon the words spoken by the guru.
